findings.text: For a shebang such as `#!/usr/bin/python3 -u`, `parseShebang` returns the single string `python3 -u`. That string is used as `parsed.file`, so `which` cannot find it. `escapeMetaChars` then caret-escapes the space, so cmd.exe is asked to run a program literally named `python3 -u`. It fails instead of running `python3` with `-u` and the script as arguments.

0.reason: When the shebang names a non-env interpreter with an argument, parseShebang returns `${interpreter} ${argument}`, and resolveWithShebang uses that whole string as parsed.file, so which.sync looks for a program literally named 'python3 -u' and fails; escapeMetaChars then caret-escapes the space, so cmd.exe gets one bad command name instead of the interpreter plus its argument. This is separate from the reference bug about the bytes-read count and NUL padding.
